questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:
Some spoons are plates.
Some plates are tumblers.

Conclusions:
I. No tumbler is a spoon.
II. No plate is a spoon.
III. Some tumblers are spoons.

options.text: Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows
Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e6b8f69742ad23ca433bbb860d6506c98779597b18d75a53c69c890983d3d46.png] 

**Conclusions:**
I. No tumbler is a spoon. → Do not follow (As, there is no definite relation between tumbler and spoon, hence false)
II. No plate is a spoon. → Do not follow (As, Some spoons are plates)
III. Some tumblers are spoons. → Do not follow (As, there is no definite relation between tumbler and spoon, hence false)

Conclusion I and III are complementary to each other, so either conclusion I or III is true.

Hence, **Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows**.

questions.question: The average age of a husband and his wife was 20 years at the time of their marriage. After 6 years, they have a 2 -year old child. Find the present average age of the family.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average age at the time of marriage = 20 years.

Their child's age after 6 years = 2 years

**Concept used:**

Average = Sum of elements/Number of elements

**Calculation:**

Total age at the time of their marriage = 20 × 2

⇒ 40 years

Present age of husband and wife together = 40 + 6 + 6

⇒ 52 years

Total age of the family = 52 + 2 = 54 years

The average age of the family = 54/3 = 18 years

questions.question: The average of 39% of A and 42% of B is equal to three-fifths of the difference of A and B. Find B as a percentage of A.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average of 39% of A and 42% of B is equal to three-fifths of the difference of A and B.

**Concept used:**

Average = Sum of elements/Number of elements

**Calculation:**

[A × (39/100) + B × (42/100)]/2 = (A - B) × (3/5)

⇒ [(39A + 42B)/100]/2 = (3A - 3B)/5

⇒ (39A + 42B)/200 = (3A - 3B)/5

⇒ (39A + 42B)/40 = (3A - 3B)

⇒ 39A + 42B = 120A - 120B

⇒ 42B + 120B = 120A - 39A

⇒ 162B = 81A

⇒ B/A = 81/162

So, ratio of B and A = 81 : 162 or 1 : 2

So, B = (1/2) × 100 of A or 50% of A

∴** Required answer is 50%.**

questions.question: A person walked from a village to a hospital at a speed of 30 km/h and walked back at a speed of 2 km/h. If the whole journey took 4 h 36 min, find the distance of the hospital from the village.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total time = 4 h 36 min = 4.6 hours

Shortcut formula: Distance = [ (Product of Speeds) ÷ (Sum of Speeds) ] × Total Time

Distance = [ (30 × 2) ÷ (30 + 2) ] × 4.6

Distance = [ 60 ÷ 32 ] × 4.6 = 1.875 × 4.6 = 8.625 km

8.625 km = 8 5/8 km

**∴ The correct answer is 8 5/8 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from Village to Hospital (s₁) = 30 km/h

Speed from Hospital to Village (s₂) = 2 km/h

Total time taken = 4 h 36 min

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f7c88935600c168e204ab077cdc8e2f1b628d0b01d1c38c600bcd6f19d279395.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Time = 4 h + (36 ÷ 60) h = 4 + 3/5 = 23/5 hours

⇒ Let the distance be d km.

⇒ (d ÷ 30) + (d ÷ 2) = 23/5

⇒ (d + 15d) ÷ 30 = 23/5

⇒ 16d ÷ 30 = 23/5

⇒ 16d = (23 × 30) ÷ 5

⇒ 16d = 23 × 6

⇒ 16d = 138

⇒ d = 138 ÷ 16 = 69 ÷ 8

⇒ d = 8 5/8 km

**∴ The correct answer is 8 5/8 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Constant Distance

When an object covers the same distance at two different speeds s₁ and s₂, the average speed = (2 × s₁ × s₂) ÷ (s₁ + s₂).

Speed-Time Relationship

If distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (s₁ ÷ s₂ = t₂ ÷ t₁). Ratio of speeds 30:2 = 15:1 implies ratio of times is 1:15.

Unit Conversion

To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60. To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.</p

questions.question: Two trains starting at the same time from two stations 300 km apart and going in opposite directions cross each other at a distance of 180 km from one of the stations. What is the ratio of speeds of faster train to slower train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When travel time is constant, Speed is directly proportional to Distance.

Distance covered by the faster train = 180 km

Distance covered by the slower train = 300 − 180 = 120 km

Ratio of speeds = Ratio of distances = 180 : 120

Speed Ratio = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance between the two stations = 300 km

Distance covered by the faster train before crossing = 180 km

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bab2e62bc296011a93d54715b26f8bdf935eabac2f62a02ba88e5fae74c5ce54.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered by the slower train = 300 − 180 = 120 km

⇒ Since both trains start at the same time and cross each other, the time traveled by both is perfectly equal.

⇒ Let the time taken be t hours.

⇒ Speed of faster train = 180 ÷ t

⇒ Speed of slower train = 120 ÷ t

⇒ Ratio of speeds = (180 ÷ t) : (120 ÷ t)

⇒ Ratio of speeds = 180 : 120

⇒ Speed ratio = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions)

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). The time taken for them to meet is Total Distance ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Constant Time Principle

When the travel time is constant for two moving bodies, the ratio of their speeds is directly proportional to the ratio of the distances they cover: S₁ ÷ S₂ = D₁ ÷ D₂.

Constant Distance Principle

When the distance covered is constant for two moving bodies, their speeds are inversely proportional to the time taken: S₁ ÷ S₂ = T₂ ÷ T₁.
